topic: A bent phone charger cable holding on for dear life.

episode.title: If Things Could Talk: The Bent Charger

shots.narration: I'm one bedtime scroll away from becoming modern art.
shots.scene: Cosy modern bedroom, vertical 9:16 composition, bright 3D cartoon style, phone beside a pillow, no visible text or logos.
shots.action: A white charger cable with big blue eyes and a small worried mouth on its connector bends sharply beneath the phone.
shots.mood: Warm bedside lighting, exaggerated worried expression, playful tension.

shots.narration: I used to have curves in all the right places.
shots.scene: Bedroom nightstand beside a neatly made bed, vertical 9:16, colourful 3D cartoon style, no text or logos.
shots.action: The white charger cable, its connector sporting big blue eyes and a small wistful mouth, curls into a relaxed loop.
shots.mood: Soft golden light, peaceful nostalgic expression.

shots.narration: [sighs] Now I'm doing yoga nobody asked for.
shots.scene: Bedside gap between a wall outlet and a phone on the mattress, vertical 9:16, no text or logos.
shots.action: The white charger cable with big blue eyes and a small strained mouth stretches taut between the outlet and phone.
shots.mood: Bright cosy colours, comically strained expression.

shots.narration: Apparently, the comfortable position is always farther from the socket.
shots.scene: Close view across a soft duvet toward the bedside outlet, vertical 9:16, no text or logos.
shots.action: A hand pulls the connected phone farther across the duvet, tightening the white cable with big blue eyes and a small alarmed mouth.
shots.mood: Warm light, exaggerated alarm, relatable bedtime chaos.

shots.narration: My entire career now depends on this one ridiculous angle.
shots.scene: Close-up of a phone propped against a plain cushion, vertical 9:16, blank dark screen, no text or logos.
shots.action: The white charger cable with big blue eyes and a small determined mouth balances its bent connector against the cushion.
shots.mood: Comically delicate balance, focused expression, soft bedroom lighting.

shots.narration: [whispers] Please don't discover the other side of the bed.
shots.scene: Wide vertical 9:16 view of the bed, connected phone near the far pillow, no text or logos.
shots.action: The white charger cable with big blue eyes and a small pleading mouth slides to the very edge of the mattress.
shots.mood: Playful suspense, pleading eyes, warm colourful surroundings.

shots.narration: Finally, somebody noticed my permanent question-mark posture.
shots.scene: Bedside tabletop with the disconnected phone resting nearby, vertical 9:16, no text or logos.
shots.action: A hand lifts the unplugged white charger cable, whose big blue eyes and small hopeful mouth sit above its visibly bent neck.
shots.mood: Gentle relief, hopeful expression, clean morning light.

shots.narration: I thought the drawer meant a peaceful retirement.
shots.scene: Open bedside drawer containing plain spare buttons and tangled earphones, vertical 9:16, no text or logos.
shots.action: A hand lowers the white charger cable with big blue eyes and a small contented mouth into the drawer.
shots.mood: Cosy morning colours, peaceful expression, inviting soft shadows.

shots.narration: [chuckles] I retired into a drawer with seriously clingy earphones.
shots.scene: Inside the bedside drawer, tangled earphones beside the bent charger, vertical 9:16, no text or logos.
shots.action: A loose earphone loop slips around the white charger connector with big blue eyes and a small deadpan mouth.
shots.mood: Bright comic reveal, deadpan frustration, snug cluttered surroundings.

episode.endHook: Next episode: tangled earphones explain why they can't let go.
episode.description: A bent phone charger just wants a little slack, but bedtime scrolling has other plans. Retirement sounds peaceful—until it meets its new drawer roommate.
